claim: CIRP measured iPhone loyalty (share of buyers who already owned an iPhone) at 87% for the March 2026 quarter, up from 84% in the same quarter a year earlier.
scope_conditions: US iPhone buyer panel, Q1 2026 vs Q1 2025
quoted_support: CIRP putting iPhone loyalty at 87% for the first quarter of 2026 ... That puts loyalty three percentage points above the same quarter a year earlier, when 14% of buyers switched from Android and the overall loyalty figure sat at 84%.

claim: Android-to-iPhone switching has held in an 11%-15% band across CIRP's recently tracked quarters, a much narrower pool than in the iPhone's early carrier-expansion years.
stance_target: Magnitude and stability of the switcher pool feeding iPhone installed-base growth
quoted_support: Across the periods it measured recently, the share of buyers coming from Android has held in a fairly narrow 11% to 15% band, a much smaller pool of switchers than in the iPhone's early years, when Apple was still expanding beyond AT&T to other U.S. carriers.

claim: CIRP's loyalty methodology asks iPhone buyers what device they owned immediately before their purchase; the article does not disclose panel sample size and gives no EU or international breakdown, indicating this is a US-only consumer panel.
stance_target: AUDITED ABSENCE: no phone-level switching evidence from EU/DMA markets
scope_conditions: Methodology description only; no geographic disaggregation provided
quoted_support: The firm has been tracking this movement for years by asking iPhone buyers what device they owned right before their purchase, among other questions about how they shop.

claim: High and rising iPhone loyalty implies a near-saturated US installed base, since only a small and stable share of buyers switch platforms each year.
stance_target: Installed-base saturation vs. structural lock-in (dual reading)
quoted_support: CIRP's numbers suggest the bulk of smartphone owners settled on a platform long ago, and only a small slice change sides each year.
